His phenomenal memory and chess understanding were recognized early, and he played 276 games in 16 months across 13 countries to achieve his GM norms, demonstrating extraordinary concentration and reps from a very young age.

early_history_summary: MenaRD began his fighting game career in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, training in a small local game center with unreliable power that made long practice sessions difficult. He started competing at age 15 in 2015, and his breakout came in 2017 when he won a Capcom Pro Tour ranking event in his home country, leading to his signing by Rise Nation. He won the Capcom Cup 2017 in Anaheim, California, defeating legends including Daigo Umehara and reigning EVO champion Tokido.
primary_leverage_engine: Constraint-driven self-creation and fighting game immersion
family_context_summary: From Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. Specific parental occupations and family financial circumstances are not documented in reviewed sources. He began his career in a small local game center with limited setups and unreliable power.

evidence_summary: MenaRD emerged from the Dominican Republic, a region with minimal esports infrastructure, training in a small game center with unreliable power. He began competing at 15 and quickly made a name for himself in the local and regional FGC. His signing by Rise Nation in 2017 gave him the opportunity to travel internationally, and he won the Capcom Cup 2017 at 18 by defeating multiple fighting game legends. The constraint of his environment, with limited setups and power difficulties, may have created urgency and a distinctive problem-solving approach. The growth of the Capcom Pro Tour and fighting game esports provided the structural wave.
starting_point: From Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic; began training in a small local game center with unreliable power and limited setups; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Professional fighting game player representing Weibo Gaming and Red Bull eSports; co-owner of Bandits Gaming; 2x Capcom Cup champion (2017, 2023); 4x EVO champion; residing in the United States.

trajectory.event: Began competitive fighting game career, securing joint-5th at Fighting Fest 2015 in the Dominican Republic.
Won Capcom Cup 2017, defeating reigning EVO champion Tokido to claim $250,000, the largest prize in fighting game history at the time.
Won his second Capcom Cup championship, becoming the only player to ever win Capcom Cup twice.
Won EVO Japan 2024 for Street Fighter 6, his first EVO championship.
Won both EVO Japan 2025 and EVO 2025, becoming the first player to win both in the same competitive season for Street Fighter.

name: Allan Alvarez
milestone_by_age_26: Set the world record in Super Mario 64 120-star category in May 2017 at age 22, becoming the first person to complete the category in under 100 minutes, and held the record on multiple occasions.
early_history_summary: Cheese was born in Venezuela and moved to Trinidad at age 2. His parents divorced early, and his step-father was initially unsupportive of his gaming but later became a key father figure who taught him persistence and discipline. He began speedrunning Super Mario 64 around 2013 and quickly rose to prominence, setting the 120-star world record in May 2017 and the 70-star world record in January 2018. He was recognized by Red Bull for his SM64 gameplay.
primary_leverage_engine: Intensive practice and online community competition
family_context_summary: Born in Venezuela, moved to Trinidad at age 2. Parents divorced early in his life. His step-father was initially unsupportive of his speedrunning but later became a significant father figure who taught him persistence and discipline.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family background in gaming or speedrunning documented. The family situation, with divorced parents and an initially unsupportive step-father, created some friction around his gaming pursuits before eventual acceptance.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Twitch, speedrunning community, SM64, online leaderboards, Trinidad
evidence_summary: Cheese grew up in Trinidad after moving from Venezuela at age 2, in a household affected by his parents' divorce. He began speedrunning Super Mario 64 around 2013 and rose through the online speedrunning community, competing with rival Puncayshun for world records. The Twitch streaming platform and the speedrunning community provided the infrastructure for learning, competition, and audience building. His step-father, initially unsupportive, eventually taught him persistence and discipline that he credited as formative. He set the first sub-100-minute 120-star world record in 2017 and was recognized by Red Bull for his gameplay.
starting_point: Born in Venezuela, moved to Trinidad at age 2; parents divorced; step-father initially unsupportive of gaming but later became a key mentor figure.
current_position: Speedrunner and Twitch streamer; one of the most prominent Super Mario 64 speedrunners; recognized by Red Bull; co-hosts the Two Simply's podcast with fellow speedrunner Simply.

trajectory.event: Began speedrunning Super Mario 64, focusing on the 120-star and 70-star categories.
Set the world record in SM64 120-star category at 1:39:57, the first sub-100-minute completion; recognized by Red Bull.
Set the world record in SM64 70-star category in January 2018.
Launched the Two Simply's podcast with fellow speedrunner Ryan 'Simply' Reeves.
Continued as one of the most prominent SM64 speedruners and Twitch streamers in the community.

name: Alex Tan
milestone_by_age_26: Set the world record for speedrunning Super Mario World in 2015 at age 19, completing the game in 1 minute and 38 seconds using arbitrary code execution, and created the Guinness World Record-holding most difficult level in Super Mario Maker.
early_history_summary: PangaeaPanga is an American ROM hacker and speedrunner known for his Super Mario World expertise. He held the world record for speedrunning SMW in 2015 using arbitrary code execution. He is also known for creating extremely difficult Super Mario Maker levels, including P-Break and the Pit of Panga series, with U-Break holding the Guinness World Record for most difficult level created. He completed Super Mario World blindfolded in 2016.
